author: jessica
source: his 2026-10-31 07:59: "Missionboard. We've have this part at a remote ground POI that needs delivered and installed in a different remote poi in the same system. Talk to person at site A, Talk to person at Site B, install then return to Site B person"
_note: PART RUN, SAME SYSTEM: a new board family, his shape. Talk at A, collect the part at A, talk at B, fit it at B, return to the same person at B for the pay.

The story: a relay station at A is being shut down for parts; its keeper has heard a man at a small site in the same system try to raise someone every night for weeks and get nothing. She sends him her last good amplifier. He fits nothing himself; the player does, and comes back to find he has already called his sister.

PARTS IT USES: place.second remote + fill late + system same (Eliza's OT-03, proven on duo_delvetest_l1), so the card and first journal never name the second site. Fitting is a deliver with replace and a placed model, MB65a's shape.

⛔ PART IT NEEDS, NOT BUILT: the SAME person talking twice (beats 3 and 5 are Ivo). No recipe does it today. Written here as the same person object on both talks; how it is spelled is Eliza's. Letter 2026-10-31.
Voices borrowed until his ear casts them. No names or places in any voiced line. Pay: med on the return talk.

FRANCES 2026-10-31 (reviews/2026-10-31-delve-MB90a.md): rework, findings 1-5 and 7 taken (the mast is half dead: it sends, it cannot hear, which is what an amplifier fixes; the light became a hum because the model's light is unverified); 6 kept as she allowed. Forced pick answered YES: the player tells him the relay heard him, so his return line 'I'll tell her myself, now I can' pays her nights of listening.

place._theme: A: a working-built site that can read as a relay station (Infrastructure, 50 POI types in vanilla).

second._fill: Filled when the part is collected, so the same system is A's (OT-03).
second._theme: B: a small working site, never another relay.

prose.name: Repairs: Signal Amplifier on <Planet>
prose.briefing: A relay station at the <Place> is being stripped for parts, and its keeper wants her last good signal amplifier fitted at a site in this system whose comms have been failing for weeks.
prose.card: Private Contract. Take a signal amplifier from the <Place> on <Planet> and fit it at a site in the same system. Payment on completion.

beats.objective: Talk to the relay keeper at the <Place>
beats.journal: The relay keeper is sending her last good amplifier to a man in this system whose comms have been failing for weeks. I need to collect it.

person.name: Bea Ransome
hellos: Come in, mind the boxes. Everything's going.

greeting: You're the hauler. This station's being stripped and sold for parts, but there's a signal amplifier here that still works, and someone in this system has been without comms for weeks. I'd rather it went to him than into a crate.

reply: Good. It's just there. I'll send his site to your scanner once it's in your hands.

exchanges.prompt: An amplifier that still works is worth more sold than given.
reply: It is. I've sold everything else in here. This one I'm not selling.

exchanges.prompt: Why is the station being stripped?
reply: Nobody calls through it any more. Everyone's on the big networks now, and a relay nobody uses is just a building that hums.
A man running a small site out here. Every night for weeks this relay has heard him try to raise someone and get nothing back.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and sets this beat's stage; the rest loop in any order, each askable off the greeting.

beats.journal: I have the signal amplifier. Now I need to take it to the man at the <SecondPlace>.
beats.name: Amplifier Case

beats.objective: Talk to the site owner at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: The site's comms mast has been half dead for five weeks: he can send, but he can't hear anything back. I need to fit the amplifier to it.

person.name: Ivo Petrak
hellos: Hello? You're the first face in weeks.

greeting: You're here about the comms? Somebody actually came. The mast's been half dead for five weeks. I can talk out, but nothing comes back, and I've been talking into it every night anyway, out of habit.

exchanges.prompt: The relay keeper sent it. Her station's heard you every night.
reply: Has it. Then it goes in the housing at the foot of the mast, and I'll stay by the radio.

exchanges.prompt: Five weeks with nobody to talk to would finish me.
reply: It nearly did me. I've started reading the instructions on things out loud.

exchanges.prompt: Who do you talk to every night?
reply: My sister, when it works. When it doesn't, the mast. The mast is a worse listener.

beats._talk: Exchange 0 closes the talk and sends the player to the mast. ⛔ Ivo again on beat 5: the same-person part is unbuilt.

beats._model: The mast is PLACED, so 'the mast' in Ivo's lines points at something there. Overtime's own comms mast model, used on 9 recipes.
beats.name: Comms Mast
beats.objective: Fit the signal amplifier to the comms mast

message.title: Comms Mast
message.text: The amplifier slots into the housing at the foot of the mast, and somewhere inside it something starts to hum.

beats.journal: I fitted the signal amplifier to the comms mast at the <SecondPlace>. I should tell the man who runs the site.

beats.objective: Return to the site owner at the <SecondPlace>
beats.journal: I fitted the amplifier and the site's comms are back. He'd called his sister before I got back to him.

person.name: Ivo Petrak
hellos: There you are. Listen to that.

greeting: I heard it come on. I've already called my sister. She said hello to you, which is ridiculous, because she's never heard of you.

reply: So am I. If you see the woman at the relay, tell her it got here. I'll tell her myself, now I can.

exchanges.prompt: Your sister sounds like good company.
reply: She is. She talks the whole time. I've let her.
Call everyone I know, once each, and then probably do some work.

beats._talk: The HAND-BACK: the whole last step, stage 100, pays 'reward'. Same person as beat 3 (unbuilt part).

_speech: Two people, two voices, both borrowed until his ear casts them. No names, places or currency in any voiced line.
